specification: IEEE 1800-2023 11.4.10 Shift operators: a signed arithmetic right shift repeats the logical sign bit, including X/Z; an X/Z count makes the result unknown.
IEEE 1800-2023 11.8.1 Rules for expression types: expression signedness follows operand/context rules; the count is unsigned and does not determine shift signedness.

overlap_with_1157.shared_change: x86 four_state.rs runtime SAR mask selects ShiftDir::ArithRight
overlap_with_1157.scope: No array query tables or other #1063 implementation changes are imported.

minimal_source: module Top(input logic signed [64:0] a, input logic [31:0] n, output logic signed [64:0] y); assign y = a >>> n; endmodule

causes.cranelift_and_wasm: Out-of-range words used the logical sign, but the partial top source word was not sign-extended before word selection/carry. Cranelift register and memory paths both needed normalization.
causes.x86: The value path used physical bit 63 without first extending the logical sign of a partial word. Runtime masks also selected logical right shift; narrow SAR masks needed logical-width sign extension.
causes.interpreter: The wide SAR implementation intentionally copied the compiled whole-word fill behavior, leaving partial-word padding clear.
causes.scalar_counts: Cranelift/WASM machine shifts wrapped large counts; scalar SAR now saturates its count to the physical sign-fill distance in both planes.

portable_cases.states: Known zero/one and Z/X signs; lower unknown bits; two/four-state mode; temporary padding checked in wider concatenation consumers. Only the oracle clamps counts with min(shift,width).
